accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The LAN handle is restricted to the fixed-common-scale path; unknown common-scale nuisance information is not assumed to have the same information-two reduction.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Any sharp-constant result is conditional on the fixed-scale chronological Gaussian path specified by H_LAN.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper establishes an average-propensity semiparametric lower benchmark and presents implementable batched designs requiring only a small number of policy updates.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv record, revised version cited by proposal
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies multi-stage adaptive Neyman allocation through a competitive-analysis framework.
The paper develops asymptotic representations for sequential decisions with endogenous information sets and illustrates batched adaptive experiments.
The paper proposes conditional-minimax-regret pilot allocation for two-wave experiments and reports minimax-regret performance up to constants.
The published paper studies stochastic-bandit regret under a small-number-of-batches constraint and derives low-switching policies.
The paper develops Batched OLS inference and establishes asymptotic-normality results for batched bandit data.
The paper proves a CLT for adaptive AIPW inference in sequential experiments and develops fixed-time and sequential inference procedures.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Sharpen the exact-b frontier with a proved leading constant or a phase diagram identifying where chronological learning versus exact-count lattice loss dominates.
Add a theorem comparing the frontier strictly against at least two named comparator procedures on a common exact-count subclass, including a computable regime trigger for their separation.
Give an explicit finite-n cadence corollary translating the two-sided frontier into a certified batch-count choice for a specified variance box and loss tolerance.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 with the field-tier every-B exact-count frontier as the kernel; retain the sharp-constant question as a separately scoped extension.
